newsitem.title: UK: Zinc market seen tight through first half 1998.
newsitem.headline: Zinc market seen tight through first half 1998.

text.p: The zinc market is expected to remain tight through the first half of next year but higher production during the second half will push the market back into balance, broker Macquarie Equities said.
"As higher mine production eases the tightness in the concentrates market next year, we expect to see a sharp rise in refined production," it said in a commentary on Monday.
Mine production is due to increase, especially in Australia at the McArthur River, Pillara and Cannington mines, plus in Canada at the Faro mine, Macquarie said.
Refined output should rise by six percent in 1998, but strong demand will still leave a deficit of 60,000 tonnes for the entire year.
By the end of 1998, however, supply and demand should be nearly balanced.
Cash prices are forecast to average 68 cents per lb ($1,500 per tonne) during 1998, with stronger prices seen in the first half.
Current prices were higher than justified by fundamentals and should ease, but this depended on how long the current squeeze lasted, Macquarie added.
Monday's official cash settlement price on the London Metal Exchange was $1,674 per tonne.
